correctness.rationale: The last-occurrence recurrence subtracts exactly the subsequences ending in the appended symbol that one can already embed using its most recent old occurrence. For cyclic run labels, repeats of physical spacing q contribute one loss each at degree q, the adjacent duplicate contributes z(1+z)^(r-1) through that degree, and repeats spanning the insertion with spacing q+1 contribute nothing through degree q. The left and right counts are (j-q)_+ and (r-j-q+1)_+, and their sum is minimized precisely between q and r-q+1 inclusive, in either endpoint order. The cited cyclic-label reduction applies to fixed run lengths. Independently, a direct upper bound avoids this citation: count leftmost greedy embeddings by discarding all deletion sets that remove the first copy but retain the second copy of the doubled letter. This discards binom(r-1,t-1). At t=q, split the word into the prefix ending at the first copy and the suffix starting at the second. Every (q+1)-window in either stretch contains a repeated letter. Delete the whole window except the later occurrence of such a pair; that retention is not leftmost. Each set contains the window start as its least deleted index, so the sets from different windows are distinct. The only possible overlap with the baseline is the prefix window ending at the first copy when that copy is deleted. In this case swap its deletion to the second copy; the earlier repeat still witnesses non-greediness, the least deleted index is unchanged, and the new set is no longer a baseline deletion. This gives exactly the needed lower bound on losses for every j. The cyclic construction attains the bound by the recurrence. The supplied finite checker was inspected as corroboration only. The statement about positions classifies cyclic maximizers, not all maximizing words.
